A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiTASK research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary Sections A-F are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiTASK experiments on PASCAL MTL, NYUD, and VTAB, together with ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1-6 and the supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use CPAB transformations of singular values while preserving singular vectors, with joint and task-specific adaptation. Sections 3-4 and Appendix A retain the same equations, architecture, and adaptation pseudocode.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same four PASCAL dense-prediction tasks, NYUD segmentation and depth estimation, VTAB single-task experiments, and motivating image-recovery example. The ImageNet-1k versus ImageNet-21k pre-training comparison also already appears in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same full-tuning, adapter, and fixed-rank comparators, including LoRA, MTLoRA, DoRA, ReFT, and SVFT. Comparator membership also matches in the NYUD, VTAB, and PVT/Swin comparisons.

E3.justification: The reported splits, task losses, metrics, backbone configurations, and hyperparameter searches are unchanged. Appendix C retains 300 PASCAL training epochs, 100 NYUD epochs, and batch size 64 per GPU; no revised experimental procedure is established.

E4.justification: The component, tessellation-size, pre-training-scale, backbone-size, and alternative-backbone analyses are retained, as are the qualitative cases. The component ablation moves from main-text Figure 6 to supplementary Figure 7; it is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same runtime uncertainty reporting: 35.20 ± 1.05 seconds for MTLoRA and 27.31 ± 5.29 for DiTASK. Neither version adds run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1-6 retain their numerical entries, including DiTASK's +3.22% relative improvement on PASCAL and +20.65% on NYUD. The quantitative plots and qualitative prediction examples also retain the same results despite relocation and formatting changes.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Equations (1)-(7), the singular-vector and singular-value-order arguments, and Appendix B's gradient-storage analysis are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, assumption, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims: singular-vector-preserving adaptation, full-rank updates, parameter-efficient multi-task learning, and the same headline performance and parameter savings.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 strengthens v1's statement that DiTASK consistently improves performance to saying it is the only parameter-efficient method to do so, although Tables 1 and 4 also report positive MTLoRA improvements. Conversely, Table 3's caption narrows 'faster inference' to the directly reported reduction in batch runtime.

D1.justification: v3 adds a direct DiTASK implementation link in the abstract; v1 only describes its implementation's relationship to MTLoRA. Hardware, optimizer, and hyperparameter details remain unchanged. Figure 5's caption also drops the previously explicit attention-mask exclusion, without establishing changed parameter accounting.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to 'Rethinking fine-tuning through geometric perspective' and 'DiGRAF: Diffeomorphic graph-adaptive activation function,' modestly extending the discussion of CPAB applications. The broader positioning against low-rank adaptation and existing MTL methods remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized edits condense Section 5.2, revise the CPAB related-work paragraph, and rewrite captions while preserving the section and appendix organization. Section 4.2 introduces incorrect 'Section 1' references where v1 correctly referenced Figure 3a and Figure 3b.

P2.justification: v3 adjusts the architecture diagrams and consolidates Figure 3's panel captions. Figure 5 is relocated, the existing component plot moves to the appendix as Figure 7, and typography and table/figure placement are reflowed. These are limited presentation changes to retained content.

improvement.justification: The implementation link, clearer captions, and added references provide modest access and presentation benefits. However, v3 introduces an unsupported exclusivity interpretation in Section 5.2 and incorrect cross-references in Section 4.2. With the underlying results and theory unchanged, these competing gains and precision regressions leave the net overall quality direction unclear.
